agency: Tennessee Department of Environment and Conservation, Division of Mineral and Geologic Resources (Oil and Gas Program)
basis: permit date (the date the table records on each permit)
cadence: monthly (the Division's words for its oil and gas data)
name: Tennessee
note: Permits to drill an oil or gas well, by the permit date in the Division's table of every oil and gas well permit it has issued (its Oil and Gas Data Viewer and Map Viewer show the same table). The table has no type of permit, so only new wells are told. No permit number appears twice, so it reads as one row per permit to drill and amendments and transfers do not appear as rows. Permit numbers run in order without a gap. 77 percent of the permits since 2019 are for wells recorded as drilled and plugged dry. The fluid is the well's recorded purpose, which changes as it is drilled: a dry hole, a location not yet drilled and one abandoned have no fluid (unknown), so the newest months show more unknown than they will. Tennessee issues a few dozen permits a year, so a month with none is a real zero. The Division says it updates this data monthly, so the last 60 days before the read are not shown. The newest permit in the table is dated August 6, 2026.
